basis: The full course coverage map remains authoritative. This is a proposed teaching sequence and numerical design, not an official NU lesson sequence, assessment policy or physical equipment requirement.

preparation.refresh: Signed sinusoidal phase, radians versus cycles, differentiation and energy/work units. Explain partial derivatives by holding the other coordinate fixed before introducing the wave equation. Link to available prerequisite trigonometry and calculus refreshers; full academic calculus prerequisites remain in force.
preparation.objective: Interpret a traveling wave's direction, local motion and energy transport using its derivatives and medium parameters.

sources.use: Transverse/longitudinal disturbances and profile translation. Two periodic snapshots alone can be ambiguous: a displacement known only to be less than one wavelength need not fix its signed direction.
Spatial and temporal wave parameters and derivatives. Use 2*pi*n for successive positive cosine crests, not pi*n. Derive direction from constant phase.
Constant tension, uniform linear density and the small-slope string equation. Independently derive the vertical force difference and check units.

Wavelength-integrated energy and mean power. The local isolated-oscillator potential argument is not used; derive local stretch energy from geometry instead. Keep fixed-medium assumptions when applying scaling.

University lecture derivation of local stretch energy, signed boundary power and energy conservation. Only the string section is used in this lesson; acoustic and electromagnetic models have their own later treatment.

Primary correction clarifying that a string element exchanges energy with its neighbors. Local kinetic and stretch energy are in phase for a single traveling wave. The two-page derivation was read; no claim of viewing the full lecture is made.

conventions.coordinates: x labels the equilibrium position of a material point; y is transverse displacement in meters. Positive x is right and positive y is up. A crest is a pattern location, not a material point moving along the string.
conventions.symbols: Use tension F_T in N, linear density mu in kg/m, c>0 for speed, sigma=+1 or -1 for propagation direction, k>0 in rad/m, omega>0 in rad/s, f in Hz, lambda in m and period tau in s. Do not reuse T for both tension and period.
conventions.harmonic: y=A*cos(theta), theta=k*x-sigma*omega*t+phi; k=2*pi/lambda, omega=2*pi*f, omega=c*k. A>=0 and phi is a specified reference phase. A=0 has no observable crest, phase or direction even though the medium's c is defined.
conventions.derivatives: y_t=sigma*A*omega*sin(theta), y_x=-A*k*sin(theta), y_tt=-A*omega^2*cos(theta), y_xx=-A*k^2*cos(theta). Constant phase gives dx/dt=sigma*c. At a crest the tagged point has zero instantaneous transverse velocity and nonzero acceleration when A>0.
conventions.waveEquation: mu*y_tt=F_T*y_xx, c=sqrt(F_T/mu). A sinusoidal function solves this equation only if omega^2=c^2*k^2 (or is identically zero). A matching value at one point is not proof of a solution everywhere.
conventions.domain: An ideal uniform string with approximately constant positive tension, small slope, negligible bending stiffness/damping and no reflected contribution in the observed interval. A single traveling profile is not asserted to satisfy two fixed finite endpoints. Transverse string formulas are not universal formulas for fluid sound or surface water waves.

energy.local: K per equilibrium length = mu*y_t^2/2 and U per equilibrium length = F_T*y_x^2/2. U follows from F_T*(sqrt(1+y_x^2)-1) expanded to quadratic order; the constant equilibrium stretch energy is the chosen zero.
energy.flux: P=-F_T*y_x*y_t is the signed power crossing a cut toward positive x, in W. For one pure traveling profile, y_t=-sigma*c*y_x, K=U and P=sigma*c*(K+U). These identities do not hold pointwise for arbitrary superpositions.
energy.conservation: u_t+P_x=0 and d/dt integral_a^b u dx=P(a,t)-P(b,t). At sigma=-1, both boundary powers may be negative; the difference still gives the stored-energy rate. Energy density is nonnegative even when signed power is negative.
energy.mean: For a harmonic wave, mean u=mu*A^2*omega^2/2 and mean P=sigma*mu*c*A^2*omega^2/2. Energy in one wavelength is mean u*lambda; its magnitude equals energy crossing a point during one period. The infinite harmonic wavetrain has infinite total energy, so report a finite interval or per-length value.
energy.scaling: At fixed medium and frequency, doubling amplitude multiplies mean power by four. At fixed source frequency, changing tension or density changes c and lambda, not f. At fixed tension, density also changes c, so mean power scales as sqrt(mu), not mu. State what is held fixed in every comparison.
energy.pulse: A translated Gaussian y=A*exp(-q^2/2), q=(x-sigma*c*t-x0)/w, provides finite energy without a wavelength or oscillation period. Its full-line energy is F_T*A^2*sqrt(pi)/(2*w). The pulse center has zero slope and instantaneous local energy, while its moving flanks carry the energy.

investigation.model: Compare harmonic and Gaussian profiles on the ideal string. The pulse makes finite-region energy transport visible without assuming periodic steady behavior; harmonic mode connects to frequency, phase and aliasing.
investigation.controls: Profile, direction, tension 0.1 to 100 N, density 0.001 to 2 kg/m, amplitude 0 to 0.1 m, harmonic frequency 0.1 to 20 Hz, phase from -2*pi to 2*pi, and pulse width 0.1 to 5 m. Reject combinations whose maximum absolute slope exceeds 0.2, a disclosed pedagogical model guard rather than a universal validity threshold. At slope 0.2 the quadratic stretch term differs from the exact fixed-tension geometric expression by less than 1 percent relative to that exact expression.
investigation.window: Characteristic length is lambda for harmonic mode and w for the pulse. Show x from -2 to 2 wavelengths or -4 to 4 pulse widths. The fixed control region is symmetric about zero with width 0.25 to 3 characteristic lengths. Show its physical endpoints explicitly. A pulse starts 2.5 widths upstream of zero and is followed for up to eight width-transit times; harmonic duration is up to four periods. No physical endpoint is imposed at the plot edges.
investigation.probes: Independent keyboard position and time probes with Arrow/Home/End and previous/next buttons. A selected material point keeps its x coordinate when time changes; mark its y separately from a tracked crest/pulse center. If the tracked crest leaves the view, report its actual position without wrapping or silently jumping to another crest. For zero amplitude, report no identifiable crest.
investigation.evidence: Three plots: spatial profile with tagged point and tracked pattern marker; local transverse time history; finite-region energy change and independently integrated net boundary input. Complete paginated tables list displacement, both first and second derivatives, kinetic/stretch/total density and signed power, plus all time-account records. Separate boundary powers and signed cumulative transfers prevent left-travel sign confusion.
investigation.numerics: Use analytic profile derivatives. Independently compute spatial energy integrals with composite Simpson panels and cumulative boundary work with separate midpoint Simpson integration in time. Run 64/128/256 base intervals and a doubled refinement in both directions; expose residuals and coarse/fine differences. Do not define boundary work from energy change or force the residual to zero.
investigation.sampling: Harmonic-only recording panel compares two snapshots and a tagged-point stroboscopic record. Choose delta_t/tau among 1/8, 1/2, 3/4, 1 and 5/4 and spatial sample step among lambda/8, lambda/2, 3*lambda/4 and lambda. Display actual samples and principal signed shift, with half-wavelength ambiguity and zero-amplitude degeneracy explicit. Snapshot shift is only determined modulo lambda; a unique principal shift requires a justified bound |shift|<lambda/2, not merely |shift|<lambda. Model direction is known from the equation, not inferred uniquely from the sparse recording.
investigation.predictions: Before revealing results, predict c, the sign of power and the selected material-point velocity at a stated initial coordinate. Correct misconception feedback distinguishes particle velocity, phase speed, energy sign and density units. Changed parameters clear stale predictions and results.
investigation.procedure: Record one rightward harmonic run and its leftward comparison; double amplitude within the slope guard; change tension while keeping source f and A fixed; inspect a translated pulse entering/leaving the region; refine the energy account; compare a resolved and aliased recording. Preserve parameters and representative rows in saved lesson notes.
rubric: Reproducible parameters, units and slope restriction
Correctly distinguished material and pattern motion
Signed boundary ledger supported by independent energy and refinement evidence
A controlled comparison with a quantitative prediction
Sampling/model limitations supported by actual records
investigation.limits: Simulation only. No official physical equipment claim, animation requirement or automatic motion. Controls reset on reload as disclosed; saved notes retain the record. Self-scoring does not award objective evidence.

instruction: Start with a tagged string point and an arriving disturbance. Distinguish transverse/longitudinal displacement from propagation and distinguish a pulse from a harmonic wavetrain.
Construct y(x,t) from a profile and translate it. Introduce wavelength, period, k, omega and phase with dimensions and an explicit sign convention.
Differentiate at fixed x and fixed t, then follow constant phase. Contrast both paths at a crest and at equilibrium crossing.
Derive the small-slope force equation and c from tension and mass per equilibrium length. Convert g/m explicitly before substitution and test the PDE by substitution.
Derive local kinetic and stretch energy; explain why a moving string element is not an isolated oscillator despite sinusoidal motion.
Derive signed boundary power and the finite-region conservation equation. Check a leftward example without changing the sign of energy.
Average a harmonic cycle and wavelength; derive amplitude and medium scaling with fixed quantities stated. Distinguish finite stored energy from transported energy.
Translate a finite-energy pulse and identify its energy-bearing slopes. Explain why no harmonic frequency or period should be assigned to the pulse.
Compare resolved measurements with spatial/temporal aliases. Explain what cannot be inferred from one snapshot or a periodically repeating pair.
Complete a worked guided analysis, investigation, deterministic practice, independent checkpoint and retrieval comparison for later superposition and sound lessons.
workedExamples: Rightward cosine wave: units, lambda, tau, crest motion and fixed-point derivative at a nontrivial phase.
Leftward wave: identical initial snapshot, reversed transverse velocity and signed flux.
Follow a specific positive crest indexed by 2*pi*n, including its exit from the chosen view.
Convert a measured string mass/length into kg/m and derive c and wavelength at fixed source frequency.
Check an incorrect candidate wave speed through the full wave-equation residual, including points where a misleading residual vanishes.
Use local slope and velocity to compute K, U and signed power; compare a crest with a zero crossing.
Integrate one wavelength and one period independently and reconcile the units and direction.
Use a non-integer-wavelength control interval to compare stored-energy change with both boundary works.
Double amplitude and independently change tension or density while preserving the stated controls.
Compute a finite Gaussian pulse's local derivatives and full-line energy, without inventing a period.
Exhibit two different signed shifts compatible with periodic snapshots and a same-value stroboscopic record.
Audit the small-slope approximation and distinguish model truncation from numerical quadrature differences.

practice.checks: At least 50 deterministic seeds per variant. Independent shifted-profile identities and finite differences verify direction and derivatives; enumerate congruent phases and check the stated first-event/domain restriction. Include wrong signs, crest/particle confusion, cycles/radians, globally false PDE claims and all-zero degeneracy where appropriate.

At least 50 deterministic seeds per variant. Independent dimensional conversions, finite-segment stretch geometry, numerical boundary power integrals and controlled-parameter substitutions verify values. Include both directions, zero local energy, amplitude squared, density-dependent speed, wrong units and fixed-source frequency.

verification.independentModel: Fifty varied profiles in both directions compare translation and centered finite derivatives at off-grid positions/times. Independently sum polygonal string stretch and segment kinetic energy; refine to the small-slope limit. Check harmonic period averages and full-line Gaussian energy through separate high-resolution quadrature.
verification.conservation: Fifty non-integer spatial windows and time durations independently integrate energy and boundary flux. Compare coarse/fine residuals, use sign-reversed propagation and include pulse entering, contained and leaving cases. Check local conservation by finite differences, not just the global identity.
verification.edges: Zero amplitude, exact crest and crossing phases, limiting slope guard, smallest/largest supported scales, both directions, invalid/nonfinite/blank input, bounds and invalid interval options. Alias tests include full periods, half periods, reverse apparent motion, integer spatial spacing and phase-shifted zeros.
verification.answers: Use existing exact, rational, numeric and pi-expression graders. Test equivalent answers, all relevant restrictions, incorrect signs/interpretations, invalid text and disclosed tolerances. Authored worked numbers and guided fields receive independent fixtures.
verification.browser: Wrong/correct guided and prediction answers, keyboard probes, controlled comparisons, every table page, resolved/aliased records, invalid inputs, checkpoint answering independent of stored expected fields, reload and export/reset/import retaining earlier physics attempts. Inspect desktop/mobile, 320px reflow, 200-percent zoom equivalent, focus, reduced motion, math/table scrolling and accessibility checks.
verification.release: Focused tests per slice, full appropriate unit suite, lint, type check and production build before integrated browser verification. Actual results go in lesson-audits.json, including failures and fixes. No independent subject review or pilot validation is claimed.
